query: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) is an unmodified α + β dual-phase alloy whose low hardness and poor friction and wear properties limit its use under extreme-service and high-contact-stress conditions. Formulate one hypothesis for an intervention that could improve its hardness and wear resistance without sacrificing its existing beneficial properties. State the intervention, proposed mechanism, predicted outcome relative to untreated TC4, applicable operating or test boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Plasma nitriding TC4 will form a thin, uniform titanium nitride (TiN) surface layer that increases surface hardness and wear resistance without adversely affecting its inherent ductile and fatigue properties.
generation.material_initial_state: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) in its unmodified α+β dual-phase state
generation.intervention: Apply a plasma nitriding process to the surface of TC4. This involves exposing the alloy to a controlled nitrogen atmosphere at an elevated temperature for a specified duration to promote nitrogen diffusion and the formation of a TiN surface layer.
generation.conditions: The plasma nitriding would be conducted under controlled temperature (e.g., around the moderate temperature regime suitable for nitriding), controlled nitrogen partial pressure, and for a duration sufficient to create a uniform hardened surface. Evaluation of hardness, friction, and wear properties would be performed under the same high-contact-stress test conditions used for untreated TC4.
generation.structural_mediator: The development of a thin, hard TiN layer at the alloy surface
generation.mechanism: Nitrogen atoms diffuse into the surface of TC4 during plasma nitriding and react with titanium to form stable titanium nitride phases. This TiN layer is significantly harder than the base material and resists wear, while the underlying unmodified α+β structure continues to provide the beneficial mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to untreated TC4, the plasma nitrided sample will exhibit an increased surface hardness and a reduced wear rate, leading to improved performance under extreme-service, high-contact-stress conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated TC4 exhibiting relatively low hardness and poor friction/wear properties
generation.boundary: This intervention applies specifically within high-contact-stress, extreme-service environments where surface degradation is a primary concern, without sacrificing the inherent bulk mechanical benefits of the alloy.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of hardness increase and wear reduction is uncertain because it depends on the precise nitriding parameters (temperature, time, gas pressure) and the uniformity of the TiN layer formation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of TC4 specimens: one subjected to the plasma nitriding process and one kept untreated. Conduct standardized surface hardness measurements (e.g., Vickers), wear tests (e.g., pin-on-disk under conditions simulating high contact stress), and friction evaluations under identical test conditions.
measurements: Wear rate (mass loss or volume loss per distance)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the plasma nitrided samples do not show a statistically significant increase in surface hardness and a corresponding decrease in wear rate (and ideally in the coefficient of friction) compared to the untreated controls under identical test conditions, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
